dict.string: GET.ride uses Bluetooth to confirm you're getting into the right car at pickup (your phone and your driver's find each other), to connect to a Bluetooth OBD-II reader so Meter Digital can read the vehicle's speed and odometer, and to print fares on a Bluetooth receipt printer.

GET.ride uses Bluetooth to confirm you're getting into the right car at pickup (your phone and your driver's find each other), to connect to a Bluetooth OBD-II reader so Meter Digital can read the vehicle's speed and odometer, and to print fares on a Bluetooth receipt printer.

GET.ride uses the camera to scan payment and wallet QR codes, to take a live selfie for your profile and sign-in checks, to photograph your ID, documents and vehicle, and to take photos to send in chats.
GET.ride lets you choose photos of your documents, vehicle and profile picture from your photo library, and send photos in chats with your driver, passenger or support.

GET.ride uses the microphone for voice calls, for voice notes you send in chats and, with VoiceProtection or Audio protection on, to record trip audio during your rides. Trip recordings stay on your phone for a limited time (usually 24 hours) and are only sent to support if a ride is reported.

GET.ride keeps sharing your location while a trip is in progress, while you are online as a driver, and while Meter Digital is running, even when the app is in the background. With Always, GET.ride also shares your approximate location about every 15 minutes, or when you move about 200 m, even when the app is closed, so our safety and support team can see where you last were.
GET.ride uses your location to set your pickup point and to share your position with your driver or passenger during a trip.
GET.ride connects to your Wi-Fi OBD-II reader and Wi-Fi receipt printer on the local network, to read the vehicle's speed and odometer and to print fares.
